Title: Questions on Play and Drawing out the Beast

Messages.Author: Ramsteiner
Messages.Body:
Hello,

Recently came across the following play, to which I have never seen
before but makes an odd kind of sense.

The game started and Player A plays a Master: Discipline card on one
of his four minions in the inactive region. Is this legal?

If not, why? It makes an odd kind of sense as the card does state to
play on a vampire. It makes no mention of it being ready, controlled,
or uncontrolled. Plus, now you have to pay the extra blood to bring
the minion out during your influence. You pay the cost to bring it out
and you didn't have to waste the discipline master or go hunt.

What is the take on this?

-------------
While in combat, you can have play as many Immortal Grapples as you
wish to help cycle them out of your hand, so I have been led to
believe. If so, can you do the same with Increased Strength cards?
And are they cumulative? (i.e. 3 played, thus any potence card played
receives +3 damage at normal or +6 at superior)

-------------
If a combat is initiated under Dawn Operation, where all damage dealt
in the combat is aggravated, does the use of Lady Thunder (a third
party to the combat) cause aggravated damage to both parties in the
fight upon her ending the fight? Or is this considered normal damage
as she is a third party?

-------------
Drawing out the Beast - a mean little Common card which is stackable
during combat and if you are the acting individual with them in your
hand, you can play them all out in one big lay down (not to mention
cycle through your library to search for more).
How is it that there is only 1 true means of stopping this card
(Obedience - Dominate required and only if older than the action
minion) while everyone and their brother/sister are up in arms over
Immortal Grapple? Which at last count had over 5 different ways of
being neutralized or made ineffective. (maneuver, thoughts betrayed,
fortitude to prevent damage, direct intervention, obedience... to name
a few)
Please note: I am not including Direct Intervention as a means to
stopping DotB as it can only be used once per turn and as it is
actually used on the rush action where you have no clear idea of a DotB
deck being used. With IGs you can at least see it coming down, with
DotB decks you don't until after combat is initiated and then it is far
to late.
The use of S:CE does nothing against the damage. Nor does the use of
the Elysium or Lady Thunder's special ability (which acts as an
Elysium). As the person who wants the combat normally does not have
the Elysium is able to play all their Pre-range cards prior to it being
tapped and thus ending the fight.
I have made some private inqueries and nothing has really come out from
it that can possibly dent a DotB except possible hand jam and Obedience
(limited). All others either provide you the capability of taking the
offending DotB minion into torpor with you or with you just soaking up
the damage.

Has anybody come across a method of dealing with DotB that reduces or
neutralizes the amount of damage received that I have missed?

Any other comments on this?

Please keep in mind, I am not looking to get shouted at. I am simply
surprised by the way Immortal Grapple has been beaten upon while
Drawing out the Beast stands in the shadows laughing.

Michael Eichler
--
Worry comes from the belief you are powerless.
(So get in there and kick some butt!)

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 17 Apr 2000 15:57:22 GMT, Ramsteiner <ramst...@my-deja.com>
wrote:

>Drawing out the Beast - a mean little Common card which is stackable

Not common. Uncommon at least. Not especially relevant of course,
but. =)

>during combat and if you are the acting individual with them in your
>hand, you can play them all out in one big lay down (not to mention
>cycle through your library to search for more).

Yep. You sure can. Rob Grau played a DotB/Aid from Bats weenie ANI
horde deck at a tournament once.

>How is it that there is only 1 true means of stopping this card
>(Obedience - Dominate required and only if older than the action
>minion) while everyone and their brother/sister are up in arms over

>Immortal Grapple? Which at last count had over 5 different ways of
>being neutralized or made ineffective. (maneuver, thoughts betrayed,
>fortitude to prevent damage, direct intervention, obedience... to name
>a few)

A few things... one, I'm on the "IG isn't broken" side of the fence,
so I don't even agree with people being up in arms about IG... for
much the reasons you state above. Having been seated directly behind
Rob's DotB deck at the above tournament, I can make some observations
from firsthand experience.

One observation is that DotB requires superior Animalism to be
effective in this fashion. ANI is naturally found on four different
5-cap vampires, none of whom are the same clan. It's also found on
four different 6-caps, 3 of whom are Ravnos. So you can't get ANI
very cheaply at ALL.

For speed, a Rush deck needs to be using weenies, so little ani guys
with skill cards are required. So you're looking at skill cards, a
pile of DotBs, some Aid from Bats, some Rush actions, and maybe some
Blood Dolls too. The Rush actions only need to be used backwards, so
you can just bleed for 1 lots and vaporize anything that blocks for
your offense.

What really ends up being a problem is that even weenies with ANI are
not very durable. If they happen to have one maneuver in their hand
OR if you don't cycle to an Aid from Bats, they come back to close
range and with +4 or +5 hand damage, you've just traded minions. It
looks like a good trade on your part, but it's so tough to get ANI out
on people that it really hurts you just as much to lose one.

Another problem is big vamps. To kill a full 7 or 8-cap vampire, you
need a LOT of DotB. This runs your library out quickly, to the point
where you just can't put enough DotB cards in and still fit under the
90-card limit. So what you end up with is a deck that can kill its
predator and gain one VP from its prey, but then be out of cards. =/
Most people opt not to play this sort of deck, as 1 VP per round is
not really enough to make the finals and the table begins to gang up
on you a bit.

>Please keep in mind, I am not looking to get shouted at. I am simply
>surprised by the way Immortal Grapple has been beaten upon while
>Drawing out the Beast stands in the shadows laughing.

...Chuckling. Merely chuckling. ;)

-- Derek

Deafness never kept composers from hearing the music.
It only stopped them hearing the distractions.

>> How is it that there is only 1 true means of stopping [DotB]

combat round ends. It's balanced by kicking up the opposing hand damage
too. Of course, Gangrel, Ravnos and, to a lesser extent, Tzimisce have
damage prevention to offset that. Nosferatu, OTOH, don't have much
available. Besides, as a whole, it's tough to use Animalism get VPs as
it doesn't provide any blood or pool management cards and isn't easily
paired with Presence or Dominate.

exploit this and to my knowledge, the 15 Bums Rush/60 DotB/15 Catatonic
Fear deck never won any tournaments. After all, if a combo doesn't
produce VP's, it doesn't produce many decks.
